conventions: Recitative ὅτι is aligned to a supplied *saying* where no Greek verb of speaking stands to license that word (15:1, ἐδίδασκον … ὅτι Ἐὰν μή → *taught the brethren, saying, Except*), and is its own `unrepresented` unit where an expressed λέγων or λέγοντες has already taken *saying* (15:5). Where the ASV writes *that* it is aligned in the ordinary way (15:7, 15:24). Rule 43's test is the presence of an English word and rule 86's is whether a source token licenses it; ὅτι is the token that marks what follows as discourse. Reading *saying* as `added` with ὅτι `unrepresented` remains defensible and is named in 15:1's note.

Supplied English is folded onto the token whose own expression it completes and marked `added` only where no token licenses it, on rule 103's test and not on the ASV's italics. Folded in this chapter: the supplied subject *the brethren* on the third-plural ἔταξαν (15:2), the cataphoric discourse-marker *thus* on γράψαντες (15:23), and *saying* on ὅτι (15:1). Marked `added`: the locative *there* (15:33), which answers to no token, the appositional *namely* (15:22), whose carrier ἄνδρας has already spent its English on *men*, and the supplied predicate *and see* (15:36), ἐπισκεψώμεθα having already spent its English on *visit*.

Distributive κατά: *every* belongs to πᾶς wherever πᾶς is expressed, and κατά keeps only the preposition word the ASV wrote. `κατὰ πόλιν` → *in every city* gives the whole *in every* to the preposition, no quantifier standing (15:21); `κατὰ πόλιν πᾶσαν` → *in every city* gives *in* to the preposition and *every* to πᾶσαν (15:36); `κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον` → *every sabbath* gives *every* to πᾶν and leaves the preposition its own `unrepresented` unit, the ASV having written no word for it (rule 36). The three are one analysis.

`Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί` → *Brethren*: the ASV compresses the vocative pair into one English word, which ἀδελφοί takes, and Ἄνδρες is its own `unrepresented` unit (15:7, 15:13). A reference comparison reports Ἄνδρες as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

Versification: the projection carries λέγει κύριος ποιῶν ταῦτα at the end of 15:17, and the ASV translates it at the head of 15:18 (*Saith the Lord, who maketh these things known*). Those four tokens are `unrepresented` in 15:17 and the English answering to them is `added` in 15:18, each side naming the other under rule 37. The resumptive Semitic ἐπ᾽ αὐτούς at the end of 15:17 is untranslated and is two `unrepresented` units, one per token, which is a separate matter from the versification. A reference comparison reports all six tokens as disagreements, and that report is not a correction.

`ἀφ᾽ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων` → *a good while ago* is split token-wise under rule 2 — ἀπό → *ago*, ἡμερῶν → *a … while*, ἀρχαίων → *good* — rather than joined into one `noncompositional` unit, as `ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων` → *from generations of old* is split at 15:21. The two renderings differ because the ASV's phrasing differs, not because the analysis does; the joined reading for 15:7 is named in that unit's note.
report: Read all 69 candidate groups and then the dump end to end, since the table is keyed by source lemma and is blind to the chapter's seven `added` units. No construction is analysed two ways without a licensing difference in the Greek or in the ASV's own wording, so there are no patches.

Near-misses checked and cleared. (a) ὅτι: aligned to a supplied *saying* at 15:1 where no verb of speaking stands, `unrepresented` at 15:5 where λέγοντες has already taken *saying*, and aligned to *that* at 15:7 and 15:24. What differs is the availability of a licensing token, which is rule 43's English-side test read with rule 86's, not two analyses. (b) Distributive κατά at 15:21 twice and at 15:36: *every* goes to πᾶς wherever πᾶς is expressed, and κατά keeps only the preposition word the ASV wrote — *in every* whole where no πᾶς stands, a bare *in* at 15:36, nothing at 15:21b. (c) Preverb particles: 15:22 gives *out of* whole to ἐξ and leaves ἐκλεξαμένους bare; 15:24 and 15:39 give *out* and *asunder* to the verb and *from* to the expressed preposition; 15:3, 15:5, 15:16, 15:25, 15:30, 15:33, 15:37, 15:38, 15:40 and 15:41 keep the particle inside the verb where no preposition stands. Those are rule 106's three arms, decided by the count of English words the ASV wrote. (d) ἀρχαίων → *good* at 15:7 against *of old* at 15:21 is an ASV difference; both verses split the phrase token-wise rather than joining it. (e) τε: *both* at 15:3 beside an answering *and*, `unrepresented` at 15:9 where one conjunction serves the pair, its own connective at 15:4, 15:5, 15:6, 15:32 and 15:39 — rule 70 throughout. (f) The decree list at 15:20 against 15:29: articular τοῦ πνικτοῦ gives the substantival *from what* to the article under rule 22, while anarthrous πνικτῶν takes *from things strangled* whole under rules 17 and 51.

The asymmetry the table cannot show — supplied English folded in one verse and `added` in another — is what I checked hardest, and it holds on rule 103's licensing test rather than on the ASV's italics. Folded: the subject *the brethren* on ἔταξαν (15:2), the discourse-marker *thus* on γράψαντες (15:23), *saying* on ὅτι (15:1), and the object pronouns at 15:5, 15:8, 15:25, 15:31 and 15:32 under rule 74. `added`: the locative *there* (15:33), the appositional *namely* (15:22), the supplied predicate *and see* (15:36) whose verb ἐπισκεψώμεθα had already spent its English on *visit*, and the four rule 37 units at 15:18. Each `added` word answers to no token; each folded word completes what its token was going to say. Recorded as a convention so a later reader need not re-derive the line.

Uniform patterns confirmed across the chapter and left alone: the complementizer of an expanded infinitive on the infinitive at 15:2, 15:7, 15:10, 15:11, 15:19, 15:20 and 15:29 (rule 85); supplied *when*/*after*/*if* on the participle at 15:2, 15:4, 15:7, 15:29, 15:30, 15:31 and 15:33 (rule 86); the juncture *and* on the finite verb it introduces at 15:1, 15:7, 15:22, 15:23, 15:25, 15:36, 15:39 and 15:40 (rule 88); rule 32's split of a substantival article from its participle at 15:3, 15:19, 15:21, 15:30, 15:33 and 15:38; and the article before a name or before a second attributive `unrepresented` throughout. The two verses already patched in this working tree, 15:3 (*unto the* on τοῖς) and 15:14 (ἐθνῶν as one discontinuous unit over *the Gentiles … them*), sit inside those patterns and conflict with nothing else in the chapter.

BSB comparison: none of the twelve disagreements is an error. λέγει, κύριος, ποιῶν and ταῦτα at 15:17 are the rule 37 versification, which the report itself excludes from correction. ὁ at 15:8, τῇ at 15:9, τῷ at 15:14 and χειρός at 15:23 are places where the ASV writes no determiner or no word at all (rules 20, 21, 23). καί at 15:8 is unrepresented because *even as* is καθώς's own rendering under rule 82 and the ASV writes no correlative *so*. κατά at 15:21 is unrepresented because πᾶν takes *every* and no English word is left for the preposition (rule 36). Ἄνδρες at 15:13 is the compression to *Brethren*. τοῦτον at 15:38 is the resumptive demonstrative, the one *him* having gone to the substantival article under rule 32; the reverse assignment is defensible and is already named in that unit's note. Nothing was changed to move the rate.

No promotion. The one case that tempted me is 15:1, where rule 43 did not consider a supplied *saying* standing as the only English realization of a recitative ὅτι. The reading follows from rules 43 and 86 as they stand and is recorded as a convention, but it rests on a single unit, the competing reading is live in the verse's note, and I have no corpus evidence on how finished chapters treat such a *saying*. A rule built on that would be weak, and the contract is better served by leaving rule 43 alone until a chapter meets the case with evidence behind it.
